old: Two separate old verbs, one meaning to plead and the other to announce, quietly fused into a single spelling over centuries.
In some Germanic relatives, one sense survives in a word for praying, and the other in a word for proposing terms.
Its cousin 'bede,' still faintly related in English, shares the branch that once meant to offer or make known.
clues: This short verb for offering or asking has a split personality: one of its two Old English ancestors traces to an ancient root meaning 'be awake, aware.'
At an auction, you do this to name a price, more specific than simply offering. As a noun it can mean an attempt, like a run for office.
It completes the phrase '___ someone farewell,' and its German cousins are bitten, tied to asking, and bieten, tied to offering.
